_comment: THE LIBRARY'S OWN CLAUSE, COPIED VERBATIM from tools/imagegen/prompts.json
rather than rewritten. build_prompt refuses any prompt whose clause does
not contain 'no trade marks', and a re-worded clause is exactly the kind
of near-miss that passes a human read and fails the guard - which is what
happened here on the first attempt.
IT ALSO FORBIDS ALCOHOL IN FRAME, which suits this batch: D19 made
Mickey's a minicab office and canon says other pubs are facade only,
never entered for drink.
content_rules.rules_clause: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness, no alcohol and no gambling anywhere in frame, nothing poured or consumed, no games of chance, nobody under eighteen and no school in use, nothing sexual
content_rules.why: Every 1980s British advert and packet is still in copyright, and trade mark was the only claim Getty won in [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch). Canon says the same: every brand, band, club, product, weapon and vehicle is fictional.

_comment: framing_required is copied verbatim from tools/imagegen/prompts.json,
as the 9 September comparison copied it, and for the same reason: it is
the check build_prompt actually runs.
by_kind.concept.prefix DIFFERS FROM THE 9 SEPTEMBER ONE and has to. That
batch made a POSTER, so 'the whole board filling the frame edge to edge'
described what it was. These items are PANELS - one photograph each, at
the resolution a poster cannot carry - so the phrase that satisfies the
check without describing a board is the one below.
suffix is PRESENT AND EMPTY, because omitting it inherits a default that
ends 'one single flat surface', which is a board again.
style.framing_required: filling the frame edge to edge

concept.prefix: the view filling the frame edge to edge,

defaults.sampler: unset - sd-cli picks its model-specific default
_comment: steps and cfg are the library's measured settings for Z-Image-Turbo
and are unchanged. cfg 1.0 is where this distilled model is measured
and where the negative channel is inert - which is why every negative
below is a backstop and nothing depends on it.
THE LIT ROOMS BEHIND THE PARADE'S WINDOWS, 22-23 September. Since the
shop glass was fixed the windows show a room, and the room was a plain lit
wall that reads as frosted glass. These are D14's 'fake-interior ... for a
window nobody enters ... not an interior, it is a texture on glass', for the
four trading bays that are not the anchor. MICKEY'S HAS NONE, ON PURPOSE:
Jafar took the wall clock and the waiting chairs out of the sheet's prompt
because the anchor interior is D14's to design, not a prompt's. Positive
prompts only: the negative channel is inert at cfg 1.0.

items.binds_to: THE LIT CARD BEHIND east_parade bay 1 (the fish market)'s window, a texture on glass
items.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. One photoreal photograph, straight on and level, of the back of a small British wet fish shop's interior in 1990, as a customer standing at the window sees it: a white glazed tile back wall, a long refrigerated display counter across the frame with whole fish and fillets laid on crushed ice in stainless steel trays, small white price tickets on plastic spikes, white enamel weighing scales on the counter, a stainless sink and hose behind, a cold white fluorescent tube burning on the ceiling, a wet tiled floor. Photoreal throughout, photographic material plausibility, a real shop interior photographed on an ordinary weekday, the shop floor empty of people.
